I read this as **borderline**, failing part 2 of the rule. The quote, date and role all check out. The doubt is whether these words are a forecast about AI at all.

**The page.** It opened. It is Morgan Stanley's article "Microsoft's Nadella: AI Investment Will Pay Off", dated Mar 19, 2026. The article says he spoke at its Technology, Media & Telecom Conference in San Francisco on March 4, in a fireside chat with Keith Weiss. The quote appears word for word twice: once in a section headed "Nadella on AI & Software" and once in a "Transcript" section under the video. The surrounding words are: "I was looking at like why are we spending so many tokens on all this right? … The smart thing that I think everybody is going to start doing in the next year is tools use. That's sort of all software. And that is the way you make AI token efficient." The page is the host's write-up, but it prints a transcript of his own words with the video, so it counts as a primary source, not just news coverage.

**The four parts:**
1. **Role: passes.** On 2026-03-04 he was Microsoft's chief executive (since 2014) and chair (since 2021).
2. **Forward-looking and about AI: borderline.** The words do look forward, but what they predict is what users and developers will start doing ("the smart thing… everybody is going to start doing"). It is half advice and half a forecast of how people will use AI. It is not a claim about what AI will do, reach or ship. "Everybody… start doing" also gives no testable bar, and AI tool use was already common when he said it. The rule says a truly borderline case stays out and is logged as borderline.
3. **Date: passes.** "In the next year" is a one-year span counted from 2026-03-04, not the undated "next few months".
4. **Primary source: passes.** It is a transcript on the host's own page.
